texts.preamble: Shamnad vs The Kulathupuzha Grama Panchayath on 19 November, 2025 Author: P.V.Kunhikrishnan Bench: P.V.Kunhikrishnan 2025:Ker:88733 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr. Justice P.V.Kunhikrishnan Wednesday, The 19Th Day Of November 2025 / 28Th Karthika, 1947 Wp(C) No. 41298 Of 2025 Petitioner/S: Shamnad Aged 42 Years S/O.Abdul Azeez, Pezhuvila Veedu, Kottapuram, Kummil, Kadakkal, Kollam, Pin - 691536 By Advs. Shri.B.Mohanlal Smt.P.S.Preetha Shri.Motty Jiby Vasudevan Shri.Abijith M. Smt. Avani Nair Smt.Jayaprabha Arjun Smt.Praveena T. Respondent/S: 1 The Kulathupuzha Grama Panchayath Kulathupuzhai P.O., Kollam, Represented By Its Secretary., Pin - 691310 2 The Kulathupuzha Grama Panchayath Committee Kulathupuzha P.O., Kollam , Represented By Its President., Pin - 691310 By Adv Shri.Manoj Ramaswamy,Sc,Kulathupuzha G.P This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission Shamnad vs The Kulathupuzha Grama Panchayath on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83628339/ 1 On 19.11.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: 2025:Ker:88733 Wp(C) No.41298 Of 2025 2 P.V.Kunhikrishnan, J -------------------------------- W.P (C) No.41298 of 2025 ------------------------------- Dated this the 19th day of November, 2025 Judgment
texts.facts: According to the petitioner, he executed Ext.P12 rent agreement with the landlord, Sri. Abraham Sebastian, for his shop room No.767 in Ward No.11 of Kulathupuzha Grama Panchayath, situated in 15.37 Ares of property comprised in Re-survey No.962/1-4-1-9, 962/1-4-1-8 and 962/1-5-4-2 of Kulathupuzha Village, to conduct a meat stall under the name and style as 'Pezhuvila Meat Stall', Exts.P1 and P2 are the Land Tax receipt and Building Tax receipt. According to the petitioner, he obtained Ext.P3 license from the Chithara Grama Panchayath to slaughter the animals. It is the case Shamnad vs The Kulathupuzha Grama Panchayath on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83628339/ 2 of the petitioner that he obtained Ext.P6 Food Safety Registration Certificate, Ext.P7 Sanitary Fitness Certificate, Exts.P8 and P9 Medical fitness certificates for the 2025:KER:88733 WP(C) NO.41298 OF 2025 workers in Ext.P3 licensed slaughter house. According to the petitioner, he submitted an application for a license to conduct the meat stall for the year 2024-25, and the 1 st respondent issued Ext.P10 denying the same. Against the denial of license in the application dated 04/04/2024, the petitioner filed Appeal No.276/2024 before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions, and the Tribunal issued Ext.P4 order, and thereafter it was disposed of by Ext.P11 order, since the 1st respondent had rejected the application. The petitioner submitted Ext.P14 application for license to conduct the meat stall, it was accepted by the 1st respondent as per Ext.P15, and the petitioner remitted Building Tax as per Ext.P16 and submitted Ext.P17 application for license and the 1st respondent rejected the application as per Ext.P18 by contending that the petitioner has not complied with Rule 38 of the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Slaughter Houses and Meat Stalls) Rules, 1996. According to the petitioner, upon going through Exts. P1 to P4, P6 to P9, and P12 to P17, the petitioner is eligible and entitled to obtain a license to conduct a meat stall on the property. Hence, this Writ Petition.
texts.arguments: But, the petitioner contends that the respondents, on 2025:KER:88733 WP(C) NO.41298 OF 2025 a misconception of facts and law, declined the application by Exhibit P18 order on flimsy grounds is the submission. According to the petitioner, the Ext.P18 order is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the license is to be issued. It is the definite case of the petitioner that the petitioner's application is for a license for a private market in accordance with Section 222 of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act, 1994. The short point raised by the petitioner is that the Panchayat proceeded with the application, as if the petitioner was trying to establish a public market. The definite case of the petitioner is that the petitioner's application is to be considered in the light of Section 222 of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act, 1994. The counsel for the petitioner also took me through the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Peter v. Perayam Panchayat [1996 KHC 77], in which it is stated that the Panchayat have no power or right to auction out the right to conduct private markets. 5. The counsel for the petitioner also relied the judgment of this Court in Salim, S/O Uounus Kunju V Deputy Director of 2025:KER:88733 WP(C) NO.41298 OF 2025 Panchayath [2003 KHC 1146].
